chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Talking his way into a room on 126th Street in Harlem
summary: He knocked on a landlady's door, announced himself as a penniless trumpeter, and she let him in; his wife was with him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, I said this is it, to -- I stopped. I stayed in New York. Y ou know. And I started looking for a place to live, and I found a place to live, and as soon as we got into it, which was well, one of those things, I was -- talk about nerve. I walked up and rang -- knocked on the lady's door. She said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Well my name is Herman Autrey, I'm a musician, trumpet player, and I've come into New York. I'm going to live here, and I want a place to stay, and I don't have any money. Would you let me have a room.'
And so the woman looked at me -- (laughs) -- she said, 'If you've got that much nerve, yeah, come on in.'

And she told me there was 126th Street, right off Seventh Avenue, in Harlem, and she said -- she looked at me and she said, 'Well if you've got that much nerve -- ' And she said -- I said, 'I'll go get my wife. I'll get my old lady.' Which was -- who was with me then, who was -- later on, she died, and I put her away, and whatnot, but that's how I got in New York. And she told the lady, she say, 'Anybody with that kind of nerve --' She said, 'I couldn't (unintelligible) anyway.'
